GoalJudgment: Current bilingual title/description phenomenological self-induction and interpretation of inductance is coherent and unchanged. No ID/source/phase/role mutation is needed by this correction. This is a scientific scope judgment, not a fresh governmental source or D acceptance.

expectations.oldJudgment: Physically sound for fixed linear geometry: emf follows local current change, not current height. Its fresh graph requirement already exceeds finite-interval mean-rate-only literacy.
expectations.successorJudgment: Retained without semantic weakening. The new first case exposes an additional smooth unknown graph and explicitly local pointwise zero. Learner must compare local slope magnitudes, sign with Lenz, and zero.

expectations.oldJudgment: The Lenz content is sound, but switch-off continuity/topology and the phrase slower switching are under-specified when read as a literal universal circuit promise.
expectations.successorJudgment: Voltage-source switch-on, retained discharge path, finite-voltage continuity and an explicit reference direction make both qualitative sketches physically defined. Slower imposed equal-total current change cleanly states the voltage-rate inference.

expectations.oldJudgment: The essential larger-L/equal-rate voltage statement is correct. Observable same-switching-history greater delay and mandatory identical measured-dI/dt delay comparison conflate distinct drive constraints and are not an acceptable independent success criterion.
expectations.successorJudgment: Two separate experiments now preserve the imposed I(t) while scaling emf, and fix U,total R,zero I0 to compare delay. Otherwise identical long-solenoid and homogeneous linear permeability conditions support design changes without a saturating-core claim.

mandatoryCaseSolutions.oldLiteralSolution: With a finite-voltage permitted closed RL route, the current rises continuously and decreases continuously after switching to a discharge path, retaining direction while emf reverses. Steady nonzero current can have zero self emf. Without a specified retained path the literal off topology is underdetermined, so no unconditional sketch or polarity claim is accepted.
mandatoryCaseSolutions.successorIndependentSolution: I starts at zero, rises toward U/R with a decreasing positive slope; after source removal it starts at the old positive current and decays continuously toward zero along the retained resistor path. Define positive A->B current and generated emf in that traversal: epsilon=-L*dI/dt is negative during growth, positive during decay and zero in steady DC. Passive v_AB has the opposite sign; any winding resistance is separate. In an unseen smooth graph, compare |local tangent slope|, not I height; a horizontal tangent guarantees zero only at that instant.

mandatoryCaseSolutions.oldLiteralSolution: For the same measured dI/dt, |epsilon_B|/|epsilon_A|=L_B/L_A. No different actual delay follows; with same derivative but unspecified initial current the currents may differ by a constant offset only. The old demand cannot legitimately be satisfied by claiming B current responds later under this identical-rate constraint.
mandatoryCaseSolutions.successorIndependentSolution: For identical imposed and measured I(t), currents coincide; generated emfs have the same sign where slope is nonzero and magnitudes scale with L. In the separate U=constant,R equal,I0=0 experiment, B has greater L/R and slower approach to the same U/R; it still conducts steady current. For fixed long-solenoid geometry, more turns and larger homogeneous linear permeability give larger linkage and L. A changed coil design alone need not imply a greater delay if its total R differs.

coverage.assessmentJudgment: All three expectations remain jointly mandatory. Rehearsing one coil example twice is not two demonstrations. The qualitative RL/polarity plus unseen graph case and the distinct imposed-current versus voltage-drive/design comparison support independent conceptual transfer. Analytic solutions in this reviewer packet are validation only, not extra learner quotas or ODE assessment.

allVariationAxes.judgment: Retained on/off/steady state, now each controlled. Tests sign reversal with direction retention and disappearance of emf.

Retained fast/slow current change; observable wording explicitly controls equal total imposed change. Same final-current axis must be instantiated consistently with those conditions, not arbitrary different starting currents.
Retained turn count, linear core and relative L. Performance now limits geometry and permeability; holds total resistance equal only in the separate delay experiment.

bilingualJudgment: DE and EN express equivalent demands in all three expectations, both cases, coverage and axes. EN uses self-induced emf where DE uses Selbstinduktionsspannung; both are separate from an ohmic drop. The same-R condition is unambiguous in the expected performance in both languages. Finite resistance is read as an ordinary positive physical resistor in the expressly resistive RL setup, not a zero-ohm special case.
